sections.skill: Find the total price with fees and evaluate warranties and buy now, pay later plans

questions.prompt: A concert ticket costs $60, plus an 18% service fee and a $5 facility fee. What is the total?
questions.intro: Many purchases add fees: percent fees (a percent of the price) and flat fees (a set dollar amount). Compare total prices, not base prices. Federal rules now require ticket and hotel sellers to show the total price with mandatory fees up front.
questions.topic: Fees, warranties, and the true price
sources: FTC (Unfair or deceptive fees rule): A federal rule effective May 2025 requires live-event ticket and short-term lodging sellers to show the total price, including mandatory fees, up front. (https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/rules/rule-unfair-or-deceptive-fees)
FTC (Warranties): Explains written warranties, implied warranties, and service contracts (often called extended warranties). (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/warranties)

CFPB (Buy now, pay later): Buy now, pay later loans split a purchase into installments; missed payments can bring late fees. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-buy-now-pay-later-bnpl-loan-en-2108/)

questions.prompt: A $600 laptop is split into 4 buy-now-pay-later payments. Jamal misses one and pays a $7 late fee. What does the laptop cost him?
questions.intro: Buy now, pay later (BNPL) splits a purchase into installments, often with no interest if paid on time. Late fees and overlapping plans can make it costly.
questions.topic: Fees, warranties, and the true price

misconceptions.D: Charges the fee on every payment

questions.prompt: What does a manufacturer's one-year warranty on a laptop usually cover?

choices.text: Damage from dropping it in a pool
Any problem for the life of the laptop

questions.intro: A warranty is a promise about a product's quality. A manufacturer's warranty usually covers defects for a set period. An "extended warranty" is a separate service contract you pay for.
questions.feedback: Warranties cover defects, not accidents or theft.

choices.text: It can be exchanged but not refunded, by law
It must be returned within 30 days

questions.intro: Stores set return policies; "final sale" usually means no returns. In New Jersey, stores generally must post their refund policy.
questions.feedback: Final sale items usually cannot be returned.

questions.prompt: Which question best tests whether an extended warranty is worth it?

choices.text: Could I afford the repair myself?
Is the warranty price on sale today?
Does it cover more years than the product will last?

questions.correct_answer: Could I afford the repair myself?
questions.feedback: If you can afford repairs, a warranty is often not worth its cost.

misconceptions.B: Focuses on the discount, not the value
misconceptions.C: Longer is not always better value
